briefs.headline: MaxPreps moves Hannan's Tug Valley match to tonight, matching the bracket
briefs.summary: The MaxPreps schedule, updated 2:17 a.m. Monday, now lists No. 10 Tug Valley at No. 7 Hannan at 7 p.m. ET tonight in the WVSSAC Class AA-A Region IV first round, the date the bracket PDF has carried since Friday; the winner plays No. 2 seed Buffalo on Wednesday at 7 p.m.

briefs.headline: Kulusevski returns to Tottenham's squad after 526 days for Coventry
briefs.summary: Roberto De Zerbi said the Swedish playmaker, out with a knee injury since the end of the 2024-25 season, will be on the bench for Monday's 3 p.m. ET match after the medical staff cleared him; Savio is out for some weeks with a muscular problem and Lucas Bergvall two weeks with a knee issue.

briefs.headline: Szmyt's kick on the final snap gives Browns a 13-10 win over Ravens
briefs.summary: Cleveland trailed 10-0 with 107 yards entering the fourth quarter Sunday before Carson Schwesinger forced a Derrick Henry fumble; Audric Estime's 2-yard run tied it with 8:33 left, and Deshaun Watson's 33-yard pass to Jerry Jeudy set up Andre Szmyt's 37-yard field goal. The Browns are 4-2 and lead the AFC North on division record.

briefs.headline: Tapia and Habroune score as Columbus beat FC Cincinnati 2-0 in the derby
briefs.summary: Gonzalo Tapia headed in a 22nd-minute corner Sunday at TQL Stadium and set up Taha Habroune's 54th-minute finish, and Patrick Schulte made eight saves; the Crew have 35 points, one behind ninth-place Cincinnati, which has one win in its last nine and two matches left, both against D.C. United.

briefs.headline: Rays beat Guardians 3-1 in Game 5 to lead the ALCS 3-2
briefs.summary: Drew Rasmussen allowed one run on four hits over seven innings Sunday in Cleveland, Tampa Bay scored once in each of the first three innings, and Bryan Baker converted his 35th straight save chance. Game 6 is 8 p.m. ET tonight at Tropicana Field on TBS; the World Series opens Friday in Milwaukee.

briefs.headline: Chiefs beat Chargers 22-6 to reach 5-0 as Los Angeles drops to 0-6
briefs.summary: Kenneth Walker ran for 128 yards and two touchdowns Sunday in Kansas City and Patrick Mahomes threw for 272 in his 100th career win; elsewhere Carolina beat Philadelphia 25-14, a fourth straight Eagles loss without Hurts and Barkley, and Buffalo won 33-30 at Las Vegas to stay a half-game back in the AFC.

briefs.headline: Titans beat Colts 26-20 for Saleh's first win in Tennessee
briefs.summary: Tennessee trailed 13-0 at halftime Sunday in Indianapolis before Chimere Dike's 58-yard punt return set up the tying score and Oluwafemi Oladejo's 14-yard return of a blocked punt put the Titans ahead; the defense had six sacks and three takeaways, and Joey Slye kicked 49- and 44-yard field goals in the final 2:03.

briefs.headline: Williams completes his first 12 passes as Bears beat Falcons 31-23
briefs.summary: Caleb Williams, back after three games out with a hamstring injury, led Chicago to a 31-7 lead Sunday in Atlanta before the Falcons rallied; D'Andre Swift ran for two touchdowns and cornerback Kyler Gordon, activated from the PUP list before the game, had three sacks and two forced fumbles.

briefs.headline: Miami rises to No. 1 in the AP poll as Georgia falls to fifth
briefs.summary: The unbeaten Hurricanes moved up from third in the AP Top 25 released Sunday after losses by Georgia and Notre Dame; BYU jumped six places to second, Notre Dame is fourth, Alabama dropped seven places to 13th and Texas fell 12 to 19th, while Florida and Arizona entered at 20th and 25th.

briefs.headline: Kings' Simmons tears Achilles in practice, will have surgery
briefs.summary: Sacramento said the three-time All-Star, 30, was hurt in a live drill Sunday; the injury is likely season-ending for a player signed Sept. 4 on a one-year, $3.5 million deal to back up rookie Darius Acuff Jr. The NBA season opens Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Kyushu basho opens Nov. 8 in Fukuoka, 20 days out, with the banzuke a week away
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association's ticket page for the Kyushu basho (tournament) lists Nov. 8 to 22 at the Fukuoka Kokusai Center; the banzuke (rankings) for it is released Monday, Oct. 26. Monday's sweep of the JSA, Japan Times, Nikkan Sports, Hochi, Nippon.com and Mainichi turned up no new sumo news.

prime.item: Day 5. Proclamation SF-1-2026, signed Oct. 2 by Division of Marine Fisheries interim director Michael S. Loeffler and re-opened this morning at 5:47 a.m. by its files.nc.gov address, made the hand harvest of oysters from public bottom in internal coastal fishing waters effective at sunrise Thursday, Oct. 15, and says the season closes March 31, 2027, under Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 03K .0201 unless closed sooner by proclamation. The recreational limit it sets for unlicensed persons and harvesters taking oysters for personal consumption is one bushel per person per day, not to exceed two bushels per vessel per day, from public bottom; it is unlawful to possess oysters under three inches shell length, to possess commercial and recreational limits aboard the same vessel, or to take them from the oyster sanctuaries designated in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117. The division's proclamations index, all six pages read at 5:47 a.m., lists SF-1-2026 as issued Oct. 2 and effective at sunrise Oct. 15 and carries nothing issued after Oct. 15; NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened at 5:46 a.m. and still dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, reads oysters as season closed, unlawful to possess, while its own footnote reads oyster season is Oct. 15 to March 31 unless closed earlier by proclamation, and the proclamation is the later document. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries.

NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:46 a.m. with a browser user agent and dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, lists red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length and one per day, under federal red drum management, with a footnote that it is unlawful to possess red drum over 27 inches or to gig, spear or gaff them; the division's flounder proclamation FF-27-2026, which the page links and which was re-read this morning with pdftotext, cites Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 3I .0124 requiring recreational anglers to report red drum, spotted seatrout, flounder, striped bass and weakfish harvest to the division. The proclamations index, all six pages read at 5:47 a.m., carries no 2026 recreational red drum proclamation and nothing issued after Oct. 15. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries, and the limits page says a Coastal Recreational Fishing License is required in coastal waters under G.S. 113-174.2, a separate license from the inland one. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 18 days old, has red drum as the main inshore target around Topsail.

prime.dates: Open; 14- to 20-inch slot, one over 26 inches
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists spotted seatrout, the speckled trout, at a 14- to 20-inch total-length slot with one fish over 26 inches allowed, three per day, no federal regulation. The division's proclamations index, read at 5:47 a.m., lists the harvest opening as FF-31-2026, issued June 25 and effective 12:01 a.m. July 1, 2026, and carries no later seatrout proclamation; the October proclamations on the index are the oyster opening, three commercial flounder orders (FF-42, FF-43 and FF-44-2026, the latest issued Oct. 15), a striped bass order and gill net and stop net orders. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 18 days old, has the trout scattered, a few on early topwater, the guides waiting on cooler water; Beaufort's thermometer read 64.9 degrees this morning, down 4.5 from Sunday.

prime.species: Spanish mackerel, king mackerel and bluefish
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists Spanish mackerel at 12 inches fork length and 15 per day, king mackerel at 24 inches fork length and three per day, and bluefish with no minimum size and five per day in private recreational fisheries, seven on a for-hire vessel, all under federal management plans. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 18 days old, has Spanish and bluefish plentiful from the surf and piers and kings to 32 pounds at Jolly Roger Pier.

NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists black drum at a 14-inch minimum and 25-inch maximum total length, 10 per day, with one over 25 inches allowed per person per day, sheepshead at 14 inches total length, five per day, neither under federal regulation, and spot with no minimum size and 50 per day under federal spot management. The reference calendar lists October as the peak of the spot run; the Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 18 days old, has black drum of three to four pounds at the bridges and oyster reefs, spot in the evening bottom-fishing catch at Surf City Pier and sheepshead in the Seaview Pier bottom catch.

going_out.dates: Harvest Sept. 1 to 14 only; closed since Sept. 15
going_out.item: Closed. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:46 a.m., reads flounder, all species, Sept. 1 to 14 open and Sept. 15 to 30 closed, unlawful to possess, and carries no October opening; the proclamation it links, FF-27-2026, which the server delivered as a PDF and which was re-read this morning with pdftotext, was signed June 3 by director Kathy B. Rawls and says it is unlawful to possess flounder for recreational purposes except from 12:01 a.m. Sept. 1 until 11:59 p.m. Sept. 14, 2026, with a 15-inch minimum and one per person per day inside that window, supersedes FF-17-2026 of March 13 and sets no later season; the division's proclamations index, all six pages read at 5:47 a.m., lists three October flounder proclamations, FF-42-2026 issued Oct. 6, FF-43-2026 issued Oct. 13 and FF-44-2026 issued Oct. 15, all commercial pound net and mobile gear orders, nothing issued after Oct. 15, and no recreational one. Flounder in Topsail Sound are release only, the 35th day of the closure; the Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 18 days old, has them as bycatch on red drum rigs and in the pier bottom-fishing catch.

sections.label: On the Water
sections.note: All four waters reported from the locked fishing.json, generated_at 2026-10-19T05:40:22-04:00, errors list empty; the file was not re-run by this desk and every figure is printed as it stands there. USGS instantaneous values for 03186500, 03201500, 03206000, 03189600 and 03189100 were pulled at 5:46 a.m. ET for the window 6 a.m. Saturday to 5:15 a.m. today. Williams River: 421 cfs and 2.73 feet at 5:15 a.m., the last point and the window low, against 587 cfs and 3.09 feet at 5:15 a.m. Sunday, the true 24-hour mark and Sunday's edition reading: down 166 cfs and 0.36 feet on the day, falling flags RIGHT on the day; the fetcher's 638 and 3.19 comparison points are the 5:45 a.m. Saturday reading, the first point of its window, 47.5 hours old, and overstate the drop at 217 cfs and 0.46 feet. The river crossed under the fetcher's 500-cfs blown-out line at 4 p.m. Sunday and is in the pushy band for the first time since Thursday's rise. Gauley near Craigsville (03189100): 1,700 cfs and 12.34 feet at 4:30 a.m. against 2,310 and 12.75 at 4:30 a.m. Sunday, down 610. 03189600 below Summersville Dam: discharge series empty a ninth day, stage only: held 10.99 to 11.03 feet from 5 a.m. Sunday through 2:45 a.m. today, then 10.52 at 3 a.m., 10.19 at 3:15, 9.89 at 4 a.m. and 9.83 at 4:45 a.m., the window low, a 1.2-foot drop in two hours read off the stage trace and not from the Corps. Ohio: Point Pleasant 24.93 feet at 5 a.m., steady flag right on the day: down 0.12 from 25.05 at 5 a.m. Sunday, the true 24-hour mark; the fetcher's 25.14 is the 5:45 a.m. Saturday window-start point, against which the pool reads 0.21 down, also inside the steady band; Sunday ran down to 24.50 at 3 p.m. and has climbed since. waters.read: 421 cfs - pushy. Wadeable at the edges, not across.
waters.working: Under 500 for the first time since Thursday's rise, still falling, and the drop is three-quarters of what the fetcher's comparison implies. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, "421 cfs - pushy. Wadeable at the edges, not across.", and the band is right: the fetcher's pushy band runs 200 to 500 cfs and the river is 79 under the blown-out line it was 87 above on Sunday. The 638 cfs and 3.19 feet in the fetcher's 24h_ago fields are the first point of its two-day window, the 5:45 a.m. Saturday reading, 47.5 hours before the current reading, and the USGS 03186500 trace pulled at 5:46 a.m. puts the true 24-hour mark at 587 cfs and 3.09 feet at 5:15 a.m. Sunday, Sunday's edition reading, so the river is down 166 cfs and 0.36 feet on the day, not the 217 cfs and 0.46 feet the comparison implies; the falling flag is right on the day either way. The recession ran straight through Sunday with no bump: 587 cfs at 5 a.m., 577 at 6, 567 at 7, 557 at 8, 547 at 9, 537 at 10, 533 at 11, 528 at noon, 518 at 1 p.m., 509 at 2, 504 at 3, 500 at 4 p.m., the blown-out line itself, 491 at 5, 486 at 6, 477 at 7, 473 at 8, 464 at 9, 459 at 10, 455 at 11, 446 at midnight, 442 at 1 a.m., 438 at 2, 434 at 3, 425 at 4, 421 at 4:45, 5 and 5:15 a.m., the last point on the trace and the window low; stage went 3.09 Sunday morning to 2.73 at 5 a.m. The rate of fall slowed from about 10 cfs an hour Sunday afternoon to 4 or 5 an hour overnight. The window high is 676 cfs and 3.26 feet at 7 p.m. Saturday. The river is 63 cfs above the 358 cfs it bottomed at Wednesday evening before Thursday's rise, cited from Sunday's edition. The Gauley near Craigsville (03189100), above Summersville Lake, read 1,700 cfs and 12.34 feet at 4:30 a.m., the last point on its trace, against 2,310 cfs and 12.75 feet at 4:30 a.m. Sunday, the true 24-hour mark, down 610 on the day, a steady 20 to 30 cfs an hour all day. 03189600 below Summersville Dam, stage only, its discharge series again carrying no values, a ninth day, held 10.99 to 11.03 feet from 5 a.m. Sunday through 2:45 a.m. today and then dropped: 10.52 at 3 a.m., 10.19 at 3:15, 10.18 at 3:30, 10.17 at 3:45, 9.89 at 4 a.m., 9.84 at 4:15 and 4:30 and 9.83 at 4:45 a.m., the window low, 1.2 feet down in two hours, the first move since Friday evening's restoration, a reading off a USGS stage trace and not a Corps statement; the Corps' Huntington District site was not opened and no release figure is printed. At 421 cfs and falling the Williams is a heavy-nymph-on-the-seam river, which is a different problem from Sunday's 587: at 587 the pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks the file records as its structure were under the river and the fetcher's read was stay on the bank; at 421 the edges fish and the middle does not, which is the fetcher's wadeable-at-the-edges line. Stoneflies and caddis are the forage the file records, so a weighted stonefly nymph, size 6 to 8, on point with a caddis pupa dropper, under an indicator or on a tight line, worked up the inside seams and the soft water inside each plunge pool's tail-out from the near bank, with enough split shot to get down in water this heavy; sculpin are the third forage, so an olive or black weighted sculpin pattern on a sink tip swung along the undercut banks and through the plunge pools where the current drops off. Wednesday's edition fished 451 cfs the same way, and the river is 30 cfs under that this morning and falling 4 or 5 an hour; the long-leader, small-fly water is under 200 cfs and days off at this rate. The fetcher carries no Williams water temperature, so none is printed. WVDNR's trout stocking page was not opened today; no stocking line is printed.

waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 2:56 AM and 3:31 PM in the sound.
waters.working: A day past the quarter: the fetcher's file carries the moon as first quarter, 57 percent lit and 8.0 days old, and the U.S. Naval Observatory's phase table, which answered at 5:48 a.m., puts the quarter at 16:12 UT Sunday, 12:12 p.m. ET, the full moon at 04:12 UT Oct. 26, 12:12 a.m. ET next Monday, and the last quarter at 20:28 UT Nov. 1, so this is the neap, the smallest swings of the fortnight, the gentlest current through the inlet and the least bait moving on the tide, with the springs building through the week toward the full moon. The surf's afternoon high has come down from 5.3 feet a week ago Monday through 4.4 Sunday to 4.3 today, and the sound's 3.9 holds, the earlier figures cited from the week's editions. NWS Wilmington has two products on the water this morning, and neither is Sunday's. The Gale Warning that was to end at 8 a.m. today is off the active list; in its place a Small Craft Advisory for the coastal waters from Surf City to Cape Fear out 20 nautical miles (AMZ250), the marine zone off the beach and the inlet, issued 1:44 a.m. today: north winds 15 to 25 knots with gusts to 30 and seas 7 to 10 feet until 8 a.m. Wednesday, conditions the Service calls hazardous to small craft, a marine product for the ocean out 20 miles and not a sound product; the wind is down 10 knots at the top from Sunday's gale and the seas are unchanged. On the beach, a Rip Current Statement for Coastal Pender County (NCZ106), issued 2:20 a.m. today for 6 a.m. through 8 p.m.: dangerous rip currents expected, which the Service says can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water; it replaces Sunday's Beach Hazards Statement, which ran Sunday only, and it is the stronger wording. All four sound events fall inside Monday this morning and none carries a spillover tag: the sound at Hampstead topped out at 3.2 feet at 2:56 a.m., is on its ebb at press time, bottoming at a 1.0-foot low at 9:12 a.m., then fills 2.9 feet to a 3.9-foot high at 3:31 p.m. and drains 2.7 feet to a 1.2-foot low at 10:04 p.m.; the last two hours of the evening ebb, about 8 to 10:04 p.m., run in the dark, with sunset before 6:30, an approximation not from the fetcher. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: high 2:15 a.m. at 3.4, low 8:02 a.m. at 1.3, high 2:47 p.m. at 4.3 and low 9:20 p.m. at 1.3, a 3.0-foot swing each way against Sunday's 3.1 and 3.0. Today's lags from the two tables are 41 and 44 minutes on the highs and 70 and 44 minutes on the lows; the morning low again lags longest, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, which stretches the drum window at the crew's spot past what a flat hour's offset would give. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 64.9 degrees at 5:30 a.m., down 4.5 from Sunday's 69.4 and 12.1 from Saturday's 77.0, the earlier figures cited from the week's editions, the second morning of the north wind; the fetcher's file gives no reading at Topsail itself. What is running is 18 days old, not a month: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report posted Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, and the feed carried it as its newest item at 5:47 this morning. East Coast Sports has slot red drum with over-slots mixed in off the surf and piers, Spanish and bluefish plentiful, kings showing more at the piers, trolled spoons working off the beach, and inshore red drum as the main target, scattered over the ICW, the creeks and the inlets, with no word on trout yet; Native Son has mullet everywhere and reds at the docks, creek mouths and grass lines, trout scattered on early topwater, glass minnows thick off the beach and the kings still in 50 to 60 feet; Spring Tide has the reds schooled in the bays at 22 to 28 inches and better, topwater and artificials some days and cut bait others, trout quiet until the water cools, Spanish pushing inside the inlet on the high tide; Speckled Specialist has Carolina-rigged live mullet the best red drum bait, trout in the first hour of light on Spook Jr. topwaters and then live shrimp under slip corks in 15 to 20 feet, black drum of three to four pounds at the bridges and oyster reefs on shrimp; Carolina Flats has big mullet moving into the ICW and the bigger reds on live finger mullet or Gulp soft plastics under popping corks, flounder as bycatch, false albacore due on the nearshore structure; Plan 9 has Spanish of 14 to 22 inches and false albacore just outside the inlet in 15 to 20 feet on small metal and epoxy jigs; South End has the bigger Spanish in 45 to 50 feet over hard bottom under feeding birds and kings in the 8- to 12-mile range. The piers: Jolly Roger reports bait thick, multiple kings to 32 pounds, Spanish ramping up, and night bottom fishing producing red drum to 31 inches, Virginia mullet, pompano, bluefish, black drum and some flounder; Surf City Pier has good-sized Spanish on Gotcha plugs, slot and occasional over-slot reds, and evening bottom fishing with black drum, mullet, spot and croaker; Seaview Pier has the mullet migration starting, Spanish and bluefish on Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs, and a bottom mixed bag of flounder, sea mullet, spot, sheepshead, trout, black drum and the odd red. The reference calendar's October pattern, spot at peak, red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum, matches the report. On today's tides and this water, a tide problem before it is a lure problem, and still a wind problem: the advisory's north wind is on the ocean, and in the sound a north wind blows down the ICW, holds water out of the creeks on the ebb and lays the lee on the mainland shore. The sound is on its morning ebb until 9:12 a.m., and the last two hours of it, about 7:15 to 9:12 a.m., are the red drum stage and fall in the first hours of light, finger mullet the forage the file records and the report says the mullet are in, so a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig or a three-inch Gulp shrimp under a popping cork fan-cast a couple of feet off the channel edge where the creek mouths drain the grass, a cut mullet chunk on the bottom at the same edge as the water gets low, from the lee bank, and the report's first-hour topwater for trout, a Spook Jr. walked over the deeper grass edges, falls in the same window this morning. The flood from 9:12 a.m. to 3:31 p.m. covers the oyster bars and grass edges, mud minnows and shrimp the forage there, so a quarter-ounce gold spoon or a paddletail on a three-sixteenths-ounce head along the grass edges and across the oyster bars as they go under, and a live shrimp on a slip cork at the oyster bars and the bridge pilings for the black drum and sheepshead, the report's three- to four-pounders. The 3:31 p.m. high puts 3.9 feet of water over the grass and up the dock pilings, where the reds go on a flooded high, so a topwater walked over the grass edges and down the dock lines on the last of the flood, about 1:30 to 3:31 p.m., then a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig as the ebb starts. The red drum window proper is the bottom of the evening ebb, roughly 8 to 10:04 p.m., 51 minutes later than Sunday's and in the dark, the same Carolina-rigged mullet and cut mullet at the channel edges; with Beaufort down 12.1 degrees in two mornings, the cool-down the guides in the report say the trout are waiting on is on the thermometer, so a live shrimp under a slip cork in the deeper holes, 15 to 20 feet, on the first of the evening ebb, and the dock lights after the 10:04 p.m. low. Oysters are in their fifth day open under SF-1-2026 on the public bottom; the oyster bars the crew fishes over are the same structure, and the sanctuaries in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117 are closed to harvest. The surf side is under both products: the Rip Current Statement's dangerous rips from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. and the Small Craft Advisory's 15 to 25 knots of north wind and 7 to 10 feet of sea on the water out 20 miles through Wednesday morning; the piers' Gotcha-plug Spanish bite on the flood to the 2:47 p.m. high, 4.3 feet at the pier, and the evening cut-bait session for slot reds both fall inside them. Slack at 9:12 a.m., 3:31 p.m. and 10:04 p.m. is dead water. Flounder are release only, the 35th day.
